title: Engineer security into design decisions: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: How do design principles constrain a proposed failure path before implementation?
focalInsight: Secure architecture links each principle to a trust boundary and a specific unsafe state.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Threat Modeling
nodes.definition: Structured examination of assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and assumptions.
nodes.detail: Structured examination of assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and assumptions.
nodes.decision: Use before design commitment and when a material boundary or dependency changes.
nodes.failureExample: An API accepts a partner callback without modeling replay or forged requests.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Name the boundary and abuse case, then test the control assumption.

nodes.label: Keep It Simple And Small
nodes.definition: Reduce unnecessary components, privileges, states, and interactions so the design can be understood, tested, and operated.
nodes.detail: Reduce unnecessary components, privileges, states, and interactions so the design can be understood, tested, and operated.
nodes.decision: Prefer the smallest architecture that meets the stated requirement; justify each added dependency, interface, and privilege.
nodes.failureExample: A convenience integration creates unreviewed state transitions and a hidden administrative bypass.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Simplicity reduces hidden assumptions and review burden.

nodes.label: Secure Access Service Edge
nodes.definition: An architecture delivering integrated network and security access controls at distributed user, branch, and application edges.
nodes.detail: An architecture delivering integrated network and security access controls at distributed user, branch, and application edges.
nodes.decision: Use when identity-aware access, traffic steering, and policy enforcement at distributed edges fit the data flow and service boundary.
nodes.failureExample: A team assumes SASE replaces application authorization and leaves a broad API role unchanged.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: SASE can enforce edge access policy; application and data authorization still decide the action.
